bucket_name.rationale: This argument identifies the Cloud Storage bucket used by the backend bucket. It is a reference to another resource and does not directly configure access control, encryption, integrity, or other security settings.

compression_mode.description: Compress text responses using Brotli or gzip compression, based on the client's Accept-Encoding header. Possible values: ["AUTOMATIC", "DISABLED"]
compression_mode.rationale: This argument controls response compression for performance and bandwidth efficiency. It does not directly change access control, encryption, confidentiality, integrity, or availability protections.

custom_response_headers.description: Headers that the HTTP/S load balancer should add to proxied responses.
custom_response_headers.rationale: This argument can be used to configure security-related HTTP response headers such as HSTS, Content Security Policy, and X-Frame-Options. These headers directly affect transport security, protection against clickjacking, and other browser-enforced security controls.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This argument controls whether Terraform may delete or abandon the resource. An incorrect value could cause accidental deletion or leave an unmanaged resource, affecting availability and resource governance.

description.description:
An optional textual description of the resource; provided by the
client when the resource is created.
description.rationale: This argument only provides descriptive information about the backend bucket. It does not directly affect access control, encryption, integrity, availability, or other security settings.

edge_security_policy.description: The security policy associated with this backend bucket.
edge_security_policy.rationale: This argument attaches an edge security policy to the backend bucket. It directly affects how incoming traffic is inspected, filtered, and protected.

enable_cdn.description:
If true, enable Cloud CDN for this BackendBucket.
Note: This cannot be set to true when loadBalancingScheme is set to INTERNAL_MANAGED.
enable_cdn.rationale: This argument enables or disables Cloud CDN for content delivery and caching. It is mainly a performance and architecture choice, while decisions about whether content is suitable for caching remain the responsibility of the team.

load_balancing_scheme.description:
The value can only be INTERNAL_MANAGED for cross-region internal layer 7 load balancer.
If loadBalancingScheme is not specified, the backend bucket can be used by classic global external load balancers, or global application external load balancers, or both.
Important: CDN cannot be enabled (enableCdn cannot be set to true) when loadBalancingScheme is set to INTERNAL_MANAGED. Possible values: ["INTERNAL_MANAGED"]
load_balancing_scheme.rationale: This argument defines the load-balancing topology used by the application. Choosing an internal or external architecture depends on the team's functional and deployment requirements and is outside generic platform security enforcement.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035.  Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and
match the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means
the first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the
last character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: This argument only sets the resource name. It does not directly control access, encryption, integrity, availability, or other security behaviour.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This argument identifies the Google Cloud project that contains the resource. It is a resource placement reference and does not directly configure a security control.

cdn_policy.description: Cloud CDN configuration for this Backend Bucket.

cdn_policy.cache_mode.description:
Specifies the cache setting for all responses from this backend.
The possible values are: USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS, FORCE_CACHE_ALL and CACHE_ALL_STATIC Possible values: ["USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS", "FORCE_CACHE_ALL", "CACHE_ALL_STATIC"]
cdn_policy.cache_mode.rationale: This argument controls how Cloud CDN decides which responses to cache. It is a functional content-delivery and data-management setting rather than a platform-level security control.

cdn_policy.client_ttl.description:
Specifies the maximum allowed TTL for cached content served by this origin. When the
'cache_mode' is set to "USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS", you must omit this field.
cdn_policy.client_ttl.rationale: This argument sets how long clients may treat cached content as fresh. The duration is a team-defined caching and data-management preference rather than a security control.

cdn_policy.default_ttl.description:
Specifies the default TTL for cached content served by this origin for responses
that do not have an existing valid TTL (max-age or s-max-age). When the 'cache_mode'
is set to "USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS", you must omit this field.
cdn_policy.default_ttl.rationale: This argument defines the default caching duration when the origin does not provide a valid TTL. It is a performance and cache-management setting rather than a security mechanism.

cdn_policy.max_ttl.description:
Specifies the maximum allowed TTL for cached content served by this origin. When the
'cache_mode' is set to "USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS", you must omit this field.
cdn_policy.max_ttl.rationale: This argument limits the maximum duration that content may remain fresh in the cache. Cache duration is an operational data-management choice and not a generic platform security control.

cdn_policy.negative_caching.description: Negative caching allows per-status code TTLs to be set, in order to apply fine-grained caching for common errors or redirects.
cdn_policy.negative_caching.rationale: This argument enables caching for selected error and redirect responses. It mainly affects cache behaviour and performance rather than directly configuring a security control.

cdn_policy.request_coalescing.description: If true then Cloud CDN will combine multiple concurrent cache fill requests into a small number of requests to the origin.
cdn_policy.request_coalescing.rationale: This argument combines concurrent cache-fill requests to reduce load on the origin. It is mainly a performance and availability optimisation and does not directly configure a security control.

cdn_policy.serve_while_stale.description: Serve existing content from the cache (if available) when revalidating content with the origin, or when an error is encountered when refreshing the cache.
cdn_policy.serve_while_stale.rationale: This argument controls how long stale cached content may be served during revalidation or origin errors. Data freshness and stale-content handling are operational choices made by the team rather than security controls.

cdn_policy.signed_url_cache_max_age_sec.description:
Maximum number of seconds the response to a signed URL request will
be considered fresh. After this time period,
the response will be revalidated before being served.
When serving responses to signed URL requests,
Cloud CDN will internally behave as though
all responses from this backend had a "Cache-Control: public,
max-age=[TTL]" header, regardless of any existing Cache-Control
header. The actual headers served in responses will not be altered.
cdn_policy.signed_url_cache_max_age_sec.rationale: This argument determines how long responses requested through signed URLs remain fresh in Cloud CDN. An excessive duration could extend access to cached protected content beyond the intended period.

cdn_policy.bypass_cache_on_request_heade.description: Bypass the cache when the specified request headers are matched - e.g. Pragma or Authorization headers. Up to 5 headers can be specified. The cache is bypassed for all cdnPolicy.cacheMode settings.
The header field name to match on when bypassing cache. Values are case-insensitive.
cdn_policy.bypass_cache_on_request_heade.rationale: This argument specifies the request header names that cause the cache to be bypassed. The chosen headers depend on application behaviour and are team-defined configuration values rather than platform security policy targets.

cdn_policy.cache_key_policy.include_http.description:
Allows HTTP request headers (by name) to be used in the
cache key.
cdn_policy.cache_key_policy.include_http.rationale: This argument selects which HTTP headers are included in the cache key. It controls functional caching behaviour and is based on application-specific response variation rather than a generic security requirement.

cdn_policy.cache_key_policy.query_string.description:
Names of query string parameters to include in cache keys.
Default parameters are always included. '&' and '=' will
be percent encoded and not treated as delimiters.
cdn_policy.cache_key_policy.query_string.rationale: This argument selects which query parameters are included in cache keys. The choice depends on how the application generates content, making it an operational caching decision rather than a platform security control.

cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.description:
Sets a cache TTL for the specified HTTP status code. negativeCaching must be enabled to configure negativeCachingPolicy.
Omitting the policy and leaving negativeCaching enabled will use Cloud CDN's default cache TTLs.

cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.code.description:
The HTTP status code to define a TTL against. Only HTTP status codes 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 421, 451 and 501
can be specified as values, and you cannot specify a status code more than once.
cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.code.rationale: This argument selects the HTTP status code for a negative caching rule. It defines cache behaviour for errors or redirects but does not directly configure a security control.

cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.ttl.description:
The TTL (in seconds) for which to cache responses with the corresponding status code. The maximum allowed value is 1800s
(30 minutes), noting that infrequently accessed objects may be evicted from the cache before the defined TTL.
cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.ttl.rationale: This argument sets how long the selected error or redirect response is cached. It mainly affects caching behaviour and service performance rather than directly controlling security.

params.description: Additional params passed with the request, but not persisted as part of resource payload

params.resource_manager_tags.description:
Resource manager tags to be bound to the backend bucket. Tag keys and values have the
same definition as resource manager tags. Keys must be in the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id},
and values are in the format tagValues/456.
params.resource_manager_tags.rationale: Resource Manager tags can be used by organisation policies, IAM conditions, and other governance controls. Incorrect tags could affect how security and compliance rules are applied to the resource.
